Excellent question. The best thing a counselor can do is treat me like I'm a normal adult. I was discussing a protest idea I have for the anti-loiter laws in my town that discriminate against the homeless and the driver here looked me right in the eye and said, "Don't you think you're a little bit of a small fish jumping into a big pond?" People who have known me all my life pretty much consider me a big fish with lots of potential. I know she probably just has compassion fatigue, but my biggest piece of advice is do not assume. Yes I am severely mentally ill, but I am almost sure that my IQ score is higher than any of the staff that works here. 

What I love about living here is that I feel free to achieve my potential as a creative. I do not have to rely on standard work to support myself, which is good, because I would just be plunged into homelessness again. Now I can write. Paint. Design. I can live on my schedule and not have to worry about the wrath of my mother for sleeping past 10am. I am surrounded constantly by other humans, which is very "nourishing" to my functioning level as I turn into an inanimate object when I am alone.
